summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, Chagas-related cardiomyopathy, and recent pleurodesis was readmitted for persistent fever, productive cough with yellow sputum, and a mechanical fall. He had been discharged recently after a viral syndrome and pleural effusion. On admission, he was febrile with elevated white count and imaging showing a loculated right pleural effusion and atelectasis. He was treated empirically for healthcare-associated pneumonia with vancomycin and Zosyn. Blood and sputum cultures remained negative. His fever and cough resolved, and the right pleural catheter was removed. He completed five days of IV antibiotics in hospital and was discharged on a 10-day course with oral levofloxacin and dialysis-administered vancomycin. His hip X-ray showed no fracture, and pain was managed with acetaminophen and oxycodone. Lisinopril was temporarily reduced and then increased back toward home dose. He was discharged home with services and follow-up plans.
